name: Torch
description:
A wooden handle wrapped in resinous cloth, ready to be lit from an existing flame.

One torch burns for 1 hour, giving bright light out to 20 feet and dim light from there to 40 feet. A hit with a burning torch used as an improvised melee weapon deals 1 fire damage. The listed price and weight cover one unlit torch.

weight.notes: Adjusted weight of one dry wooden torch with its resinous wrapping; nothing is treated as weightless.

source.title: Devil's Table: Goods & Provisions
source.reference: 2014 SRD 5.1, Adventuring Gear: Torch. Attack and token light are adjudicated manually. Original wording; project prices and adjusted weights. See docs/GENERAL_STORE_REVIEW.md.
source.license: Original project text: distribution license pending; referenced SRD 5.1 rules: CC-BY-4.0.

use.name: Mark one torch burned out
use.condition: Use only after one torch is fully exhausted; ignition and remaining burn time are tracked manually.

name: Candle
description:
A short candle made from an economical blend of wax and rendered fat. It is a cheap source of light for a bedside, shrine or sheltered workbench.

One candle burns for 1 hour, giving bright light out to 5 feet and dim light from there to 10 feet. It has no holder and is easily extinguished by a gust.

weight.notes: Adjusted weight for one small candle, including its wick; holder and protective lantern are separate.

source.title: Devil's Table: Goods & Provisions
source.reference: 2014 SRD 5.1, Adventuring Gear: Candle. Original wording; project prices and adjusted weights. See docs/GENERAL_STORE_REVIEW.md.
source.license: Original project text: distribution license pending; referenced SRD 5.1 rules: CC-BY-4.0.

use.name: Mark one candle burned out
use.condition: Use only when this candle is exhausted; lighting it does not consume it immediately.

name: Beeswax Candle
description:
A clean-burning beeswax candle with a plaited wick and a faint honey scent. Its slower burn makes it a favoured purchase for a long evening indoors.

This project variant burns for 4 hours, giving bright light out to 5 feet and dim light from there to 10 feet. Sold singly without a holder. Its material improves convenience, not light radius.

weight.notes: Adjusted weight for one long beeswax candle; extra wax accounts for its longer burn.

source.title: Devil's Table: Goods & Provisions
source.reference: 2014 SRD 5.1 Candle light distances; four-hour duration is a Devil's Table variant. Original wording; project prices and adjusted weights. See docs/GENERAL_STORE_REVIEW.md.
source.license: Original project text: distribution license pending; referenced SRD 5.1 rules: CC-BY-4.0.

use.name: Mark one beeswax candle burned out
use.condition: Use only after the entire four-hour candle is spent; track partial burning manually.

name: Tallow Candle
description:
A thick candle of rendered tallow around a twisted wick. It is inexpensive but gives off more smell and smoke than beeswax, especially when the wick needs trimming.

This project variant burns for 2 hours, giving bright light out to 5 feet and dim light from there to 10 feet. Sold singly without a holder; keep it sheltered from wind.

weight.notes: Adjusted weight for a thicker tallow candle and wick, with no holder included.

source.title: Devil's Table: Goods & Provisions
source.reference: 2014 SRD 5.1 Candle light distances; two-hour duration is a Devil's Table variant. Original wording; project prices and adjusted weights. See docs/GENERAL_STORE_REVIEW.md.
source.license: Original project text: distribution license pending; referenced SRD 5.1 rules: CC-BY-4.0.

use.name: Mark one tallow candle burned out
use.condition: Use only after the entire two-hour candle is spent; track partial burning manually.

name: Lantern
description:
A simple tin lantern with translucent horn panels, a carrying ring and a socket for one candle. It shields the flame from ordinary draughts but cannot close down to a narrow beam.

Sold without a candle. With a standard Candle it gives bright light out to 5 feet and dim light from there to 10 feet for 1 hour. Beeswax and tallow candles retain their own burn times. Add the loaded candle's weight separately; the lantern itself is reusable.

weight.notes: Adjusted empty weight for the tin frame and horn panels; excludes the candle.

source.title: Devil's Table: Goods & Provisions
source.reference: Original candle-lantern design using the 2014 Candle light profile. Original wording; project prices and adjusted weights. See docs/GENERAL_STORE_REVIEW.md.
source.license: Original project content; distribution license pending.

use.name: Light candle lantern
use.condition: Requires a separately carried candle and a means of ignition; track its burn time and weight separately.

name: Hooded Lantern
description:
A metal oil lantern with glass panes and a sliding hood. It is built for travellers who need a useful light that can be screened quickly.

With 1 pint of oil it burns for 6 hours, giving bright light out to 30 feet and dim light from there to 60 feet. Lowering the hood takes an action and leaves only dim light within 5 feet. Sold with a wick but no oil; fuel weight is additional.

weight.notes: Adjusted empty weight includes metalwork, glass and wick; excludes the oil supply.

source.title: Devil's Table: Goods & Provisions
source.reference: 2014 SRD 5.1, Adventuring Gear: Lantern, Hooded. Original wording; project prices and adjusted weights. See docs/GENERAL_STORE_REVIEW.md.
source.license: Original project text: distribution license pending; referenced SRD 5.1 rules: CC-BY-4.0.

use.name: Light hooded lantern
use.condition: Requires oil and ignition. Set normal or hooded light manually; consume fuel separately.

name: Bullseye Lantern
description:
A sturdy oil lantern with a reflector and a polished lens that concentrates its light into a forward beam. It is useful when inspecting a passage or signalling along a road.

A pint of oil supplies 6 hours of burning. The cone is brightly lit to 60 feet, with dim light extending from there to 120 feet. The beam does not light the space behind the bearer. Sold with a wick and without oil; fuel weight is additional.

weight.notes: Adjusted empty weight includes the heavier lens, reflector, frame and wick; excludes oil.

source.title: Devil's Table: Goods & Provisions
source.reference: 2014 SRD 5.1, Adventuring Gear: Lantern, Bullseye. Original wording; project prices and adjusted weights. See docs/GENERAL_STORE_REVIEW.md.
source.license: Original project text: distribution license pending; referenced SRD 5.1 rules: CC-BY-4.0.

use.name: Light bullseye lantern
use.condition: Requires oil and ignition. Aim and configure the light cone manually; consume fuel separately.

name: Lamp
description:
A small glazed lamp with a shallow oil reservoir and a replaceable wick. It sits securely on a table but has no enclosure to protect its flame while travelling.

One pint of oil supplies 6 hours of light: bright within 15 feet, then dim out to a total distance of 45 feet. Sold with a wick but no fuel. Carry it upright and account for loaded oil separately.

weight.notes: Adjusted empty weight of a small ceramic lamp and wick; oil is additional.

source.title: Devil's Table: Goods & Provisions
source.reference: 2014 SRD 5.1, Adventuring Gear: Lamp. Original wording; project prices and adjusted weights. See docs/GENERAL_STORE_REVIEW.md.
source.license: Original project text: distribution license pending; referenced SRD 5.1 rules: CC-BY-4.0.

use.name: Light oil lamp
use.condition: Requires oil, ignition and a stable surface; configure lighting and account for fuel manually.

name: Lamp Oil
description:
A stoppered clay flask of ordinary lamp oil. One pint supplies an oil lamp, hooded lantern or bullseye lantern for 6 hours; the entire filled flask is included in the listed weight.

As an action, oil can be splashed within 5 feet or thrown up to 20 feet, using an improvised ranged attack against a creature or object. On a hit it coats the target for 1 minute; fire damage during that time adds 5 fire damage from the oil. A pint spread across a level 5-foot square burns for 2 rounds when ignited, dealing 5 fire damage when a creature enters or ends its turn there, at most once per turn. These combat uses require manual resolution.

If the empty flask is retained after pouring, track it separately at 0.25 lb; transferred oil weighs 0.75 lb.
saleUnit: one stoppered flask containing 1 pint of oil

weight.notes: Adjusted total: 0.75 lb of oil plus a 0.25 lb clay flask and stopper. Do not count both the full flask and transferred oil.

source.title: Devil's Table: Goods & Provisions
source.reference: 2014 SRD 5.1, Adventuring Gear: Oil. Prices, filled weight and packaging allowance are project values. Original wording; project prices and adjusted weights. See docs/GENERAL_STORE_REVIEW.md.
source.license: Original project text: distribution license pending; referenced SRD 5.1 rules: CC-BY-4.0.

use.name: Use one pint of oil
use.condition: Records one whole pint being poured or expended. Track transferred fuel and any retained empty flask separately.

name: Tinderbox
description:
A small lidded box holding flint, a striking steel and dry tinder. Keeping the tinder dry matters more than a fine finish on the case.

Using it to light a torch or other plentiful exposed fuel takes an action. Starting another sort of fire takes 1 minute. The listed price includes the reusable tools and a modest starting supply of tinder; replace damp or exhausted tinder as needed.

weight.notes: Adjusted total for the small box, flint, steel and a starting pinch of tinder.

source.title: Devil's Table: Goods & Provisions
source.reference: 2014 SRD 5.1, Adventuring Gear: Tinderbox. Original wording; project prices and adjusted weights. See docs/GENERAL_STORE_REVIEW.md.

name: Flint & Steel
description:
A sharp piece of flint paired with a curved striking steel. Proper blows throw sparks into suitable dry tinder.

Sold as a matched pair without tinder or a storage box. This is a replacement or stripped-down fire-making set, not a complete tinderbox. It cannot start a fire without suitable tinder and fuel, and does not grant a skill bonus.
saleUnit: one flint and one striking steel

weight.notes: Adjusted weight of one flint and its small striking steel; no tinder box or fuel included.

source.title: Devil's Table: Goods & Provisions
source.reference: Original project design. Original wording; project prices and adjusted weights. See docs/GENERAL_STORE_REVIEW.md.

name: Charcoal
description:
A tied sack of dry hardwood charcoal for a brazier, cook fire or small workshop hearth. It makes less smoke than green wood once properly burning.

The purchase contains 5 lb of charcoal; the light disposable wrapping is included in that adjusted weight. Fuel needs depend on the hearth and work being done, so this bag has no fixed universal burn time. It is fuel rather than a portable light source.

weight.notes: Adjusted sale weight for the whole bag and its contents; most of the weight is actual fuel.

source.title: Devil's Table: Goods & Provisions
source.reference: Original project design. Original wording; project prices and adjusted weights. See docs/GENERAL_STORE_REVIEW.md.
source.license: Original project content; distribution license pending.

use.name: Use up one bag of charcoal
use.condition: Use only after the full 5 lb bag is expended; track partial fuel use manually.

name: Kindling
description:
Thin splits of dry softwood catch a prepared flame and help establish a cooking fire. The bundle supplies small starting pieces rather than enough fuel for a full night's fire.

Keep it dry. Tinder and a means of ignition are separate; damp conditions and the time needed to light a fire remain matters for the GM.
saleUnit: One tied one-pound bundle of dry split kindling

weight.notes: One pound for the complete dry bundle and light binding cord.

source.title: Devil's Table: Goods & Provisions
source.reference: Original project design. Original wording, project price and adjusted weight. See docs/SPRINT_3_REVIEW.md.
source.license: Original project content; distribution license pending.

use.name: Record kindling bundle used
use.condition: Use only after the complete sale unit has been consumed; track partial use manually.

name: Lamp Wick
description:
A yard of loosely woven cotton braid for replacing the wick in an ordinary oil lamp or compatible lantern. Cut a length to suit the holder and soak the working end in its fuel.

Oil and the light itself are separate purchases. The wick supplies neither extra light range nor a longer burn time than the lamp's listed fuel allowance.
saleUnit: One yard of woven cotton lamp wick

weight.notes: A light cotton strip sold by the yard; offcuts remain part of this sale unit.

source.title: Devil's Table: Goods & Provisions

name: Candle Holder
description:
A low iron cup and wide drip tray hold one ordinary candle upright on a level surface. A small handle lets the holder be moved after the metal has cooled.

The candle is separate. This open holder offers no protection against wind and does not improve the candle's light or burning time.
saleUnit: One iron candle holder with drip tray

weight.notes: A compact iron holder and tray, without a candle.

source.title: Devil's Table: Goods & Provisions

name: Candle Snuffer
description:
A small brass cone on a slender handle fits over a candle flame to smother it without blowing hot wax across a table. It is useful where several candles are kept burning indoors.

This is a household implement for reachable small flames, not a way to extinguish a large fire or alter a light's remaining fuel.
saleUnit: One brass bell snuffer on a short handle

weight.notes: Thin brass cone and short handle; no candle or holder included.

source.title: Devil's Table: Goods & Provisions
source.reference: Original project design. Original wording, project price and adjusted weight. See docs/SPRINT_3_REVIEW.md.
source.license: Original project content; distribution license pending.

name: Firewood
description:
Seasoned split logs tied into a carryable bundle for a hearth or cooking fire. Dry wood burns more readily than fresh-cut timber, but its useful duration depends on the fire, weather and the size of the heated space.

Kindling and ignition supplies are separate. Mark the bundle spent after its wood has been burned; a partial bundle needs manual tracking.
saleUnit: One tied ten-pound bundle of seasoned firewood

weight.notes: Ten pounds of dry fuel including the negligible tying cord; bulky supplies retain meaningful carried mass.
